findings.highlight: easily cuts off the large spell the person launches.
findings.evidenceJa: 敵が放った大魔術を、事もなげに消滅させた。
findings.governingReading: Saber effortlessly causes the enemy’s major spell to vanish.
findings.explanation: “Cuts off” replaces magical negation or annihilation with an ambiguous physical interruption.

findings.highlight: Father could use one as strong as that
findings.evidenceJa: 威力だけなら切嗣だって負けてはいない
findings.governingReading: In raw power even Kiritsugu would not compare unfavorably.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the named comparison with “Father,” weakening the explicit Kiritsugu reference and treating a non-biological relationship title as his name.

findings.highlight: Thank God I can’t see her sword.
findings.evidenceJa: 視えないという事は、精神的に良かったのかもしれない。
findings.governingReading: Shirou thinks its invisibility may have been psychologically fortunate because he cannot see whether it is bloodied.
findings.explanation: The English adds a religious exclamation and deletes the tentative psychological explanation.

findings.highlight: Preparing myself to do my best to stop her.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女を止めるのなら全力で挑まなければ止められまい、と覚悟して。
findings.governingReading: He steels himself that stopping Saber will require challenging her with everything he has, and even then may be impossible.
findings.explanation: The fragment weakens a confrontation requiring total commitment into merely doing his best and omits the negative expectation.

findings.highlight: I’m not so good-natured as to release someone who came to attack me.
findings.evidenceJa: 襲ってきた相手に情を移すほどお人好しじゃないぞ、俺。
findings.governingReading: Shirou says he is not so softhearted that he sympathizes with someone who attacked him.
findings.explanation: The English invents a decision to release the attacker, obscuring that his objection is not based on sympathy.

findings.highlight: Saber suddenly concentrates her attention on her sword.
findings.evidenceJa: とっさに剣に力を込めるセイバー。
findings.governingReading: Saber instantly puts strength into her sword, preparing to resume the attack.
findings.explanation: The English changes physical pressure and imminent violence into mental attention.

findings.highlight: would betray her Master
findings.evidenceJa: 主に逆らうっていうんだ
findings.governingReading: Rin taunts Saber for defying or disobeying her master.
findings.explanation: Betrayal is a materially stronger change of allegiance than the immediate refusal to obey.

findings.highlight: lowers her sword and relaxes.
findings.evidenceJa: 剣を下げ、手の平から力を抜いた。
findings.governingReading: Saber lowers the sword and releases the force in her palm.
findings.explanation: Generic relaxation removes the hand action that marks her dismissal or cessation of the invisible weapon.

findings.highlight:
definitely
definitely-WHAAAAAAT…!?
findings.evidenceJa: 間違いなく
findings.governingReading: The sulking person is unmistakably someone Shirou recognizes, leading into his spoken realization that she is Tohsaka.
findings.explanation: The English duplicates “definitely” and inserts a scream-like recognition before the following line supplies the actual reaction.

findings.highlight: a big smile
findings.evidenceJa: 極上の笑み
findings.governingReading: Rin answers with an exquisitely polished smile.
findings.explanation: Big describes size rather than the unnervingly perfect quality of her social mask.

findings.highlight: She glares at me.
findings.evidenceJa: 敵意を込めて睨まれる。
findings.governingReading: Rin fixes him with a glare filled with hostility.
findings.explanation: The English omits the hostility that sharply replaces her prior polished smile.

findings.highlight: whom I admire, Tohsaka Rin.
findings.evidenceJa: 一応憧れていた遠坂凛
findings.governingReading: Rin is someone he had, at least in a qualified sense, admired from school.
findings.explanation: The English removes the qualification and tense, making the admiration unreserved and current after her image has changed.

findings.highlight: transfer part of their body into something and summon it as another self.
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術師の体の一部を他者に移植し、分身として使役される
findings.governingReading: A part of the magus’s body is transplanted into another being, which is then commanded as an extension or double.
findings.explanation: The English replaces transplantation into another being with an unclear transfer “into something” and invents summoning as the operation.

findings.highlight: I don’t have the Magic Circuit to summon a familiar.
findings.evidenceJa: 使い魔を使役するだけの魔術回路もない。
findings.governingReading: Shirou believes he lacks sufficient Magic Circuits even to command a familiar.
findings.explanation: The English changes command or maintenance into summoning and reduces plural circuitry/capacity to a single circuit.

findings.highlight:
I’m sure Tohsaka didn’t know that I knew magic.
the Tohsakas were magi, and I don’t think Tohsaka knew that the Emiyas were a family of magi either.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂の方も俺が魔術を習っている、なんて知らなかったに違いない。
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese line has Shirou infer that Rin surely did not know he was learning Magecraft; an alternate line instead frames reciprocal ignorance between families.
findings.explanation: mirror moon prints both variants, producing two differently scoped claims with different certainty instead of selecting the active source reading.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka walks over to the broken window.
findings.evidenceJa: 何が嬉しいのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou notes that Rin seems pleased for some reason as she walks toward the broken glass.
findings.explanation: The English omits the emotional observation that colors her response to his refusal to posture.

findings.highlight: takes a look at it
findings.evidenceJa: ほんの少しだけまじまじと観察し
findings.governingReading: Rin examines the glass intently, though only very briefly.
findings.explanation: The English removes both concentrated scrutiny and its deliberately short duration.

findings.highlight: I’m glad you fixed it.
findings.evidenceJa: 直してくれて感謝してる
findings.governingReading: Shirou explicitly thanks Rin for repairing the window.
findings.explanation: Gladness reports his internal satisfaction instead of performing the gratitude that answers her concern with propriety.

findings.highlight: She’s so beautiful usually, so she looks pretty scary now.
findings.evidenceJa: なまじ美人なだけ、黙り込むと迫力あるぞ、こいつ。
findings.governingReading: Precisely because Rin is such a beauty, her silence has intimidating force.
findings.explanation: “Beautiful usually” invents a temporal contrast and implies she ceases to look beautiful, rather than beauty intensifying her silence.

findings.highlight: Strengthening… that’s an awfully odd magic.
findings.evidenceJa: 強化って……また、なんとも半端なのを使うのね。
findings.governingReading: Rin calls his use of Strengthening remarkably half-baked or incomplete.
findings.explanation: Odd changes an evaluation of inadequacy into one of strangeness and distorts her technical judgment.

findings.highlight:
I haven’t been playing around.
I know I’m an amateur, but I don’t think it matters right now.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺だって遊んでたワケじゃない。
こっちが未熟なのは事実だけど、それとこれとは話が別だと思う。
findings.governingReading: Shirou objects that he has not neglected his training; his immaturity is real, but it is a separate matter from lack of effort.
findings.explanation: “Doesn’t matter right now” removes the distinction between effort and resulting skill that motivates his anger.

findings.highlight: The Command Spell is an item of unconditional obedience.
findings.evidenceJa: 令呪は絶対命令権なの。
findings.governingReading: A Command Spell constitutes an absolute right of command over the Servant.
findings.explanation: Calling it an item of obedience loses the allocation of command authority and who possesses it.

findings.highlight: It’s fundamental in the Holy Grail War for Masters to kill other Masters.
findings.evidenceJa: マスターが他のマスターを倒すのが聖杯戦争の基本
findings.governingReading: Rin states that the basic form of the war is for Masters to defeat other Masters.
findings.explanation: The English repeatedly narrows defeat to killing, making her introductory rule more absolute and lethal than stated.

findings.highlight: won’t end until you kill all other Masters.
findings.evidenceJa: 他のマスターを一人残らず倒すまで終わらない
findings.governingReading: The contest does not end until every other Master has been defeated.
findings.explanation: The English again changes elimination or defeat into mandatory killing.

findings.highlight: description is too brief for me to understand.
findings.evidenceJa: 説明は簡潔すぎて、実感を得るには遠すぎた。
findings.governingReading: Rin’s explanation is too terse and remote for Shirou to acquire any felt sense of the war.
findings.explanation: The English turns lack of experiential reality into failure of intellectual comprehension, although he has just summarized the rules.

findings.highlight: made into artificial gods.
findings.evidenceJa: 擬似的な神さまになったモノたちなんでしょうね
findings.governingReading: Rin conjectures that worship has made them something like pseudo-gods.
findings.explanation: Artificial gods implies deliberate fabrication and removes her conjectural “probably.”

findings.highlight: supplicating ghosts uses heroic spirits to make miracles happen.
findings.evidenceJa: 降霊術とか口寄せとか、そういう一般的な“霊を扱う魔術”
findings.governingReading: Common spirit-working Magecraft such as spirit invocation and mediumistic summoning.
findings.explanation: The English collapses the category to “Ghost Magic” and mistranslates the two example practices as supplication.

findings.highlight: the Servants are familiars of the heroes themselves.
findings.evidenceJa: 英霊本体を直接連れてきて使い魔にする。
findings.governingReading: A Servant system directly brings the Heroic Spirit itself and makes it a familiar.
findings.explanation: The English makes the Servant a familiar belonging to a separate hero, reversing the identity relation.

findings.highlight: If I hadn’t withdrawn him by force, he would have had his head chopped off.
findings.evidenceJa: あと少し強制撤去が遅かったら一撃で消滅してたわ
findings.governingReading: Rin says a slightly later forced withdrawal would have resulted in annihilation by that one blow.
findings.explanation: mirror moon inserts a competing decapitation outcome before the source-faithful annihilation line.

findings.highlight: must kill all the other Masters
findings.evidenceJa: 他のマスターを倒さなければならない。
findings.governingReading: Masters must use their Servants to defeat the other Masters.
findings.explanation: Kill all again converts defeat into an exceptionless death requirement.

findings.highlight: That’s not something I know about, nor should I answer.
findings.evidenceJa: わたしが知るべき事でもないし、答えてあげる事でもない。
findings.governingReading: Rin says it is neither something she ought to know nor something she ought to answer for him.
findings.explanation: The English states present ignorance rather than her normative boundary on what is hers to know.

findings.highlight: you have a good personality too.
findings.evidenceJa: 風格も十分
findings.governingReading: Rin judges Saber to possess ample dignity or commanding presence.
findings.explanation: Personality changes an observable heroic bearing into a general moral or temperamental evaluation.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka clenches her fists with anger.
findings.evidenceJa: 悔しそうに拳を握る遠坂。
findings.governingReading: Rin clenches her fist in visible frustration or regret at not having summoned Saber.
findings.explanation: Anger assigns a different emotion and target to the gesture.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka certainly shows no openings, just like a devil.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂は、鬼みたいに容赦がない。
findings.governingReading: Issei was right that Rin is merciless like an ogre or demon.
findings.explanation: “Shows no openings” turns lack of mercy into combat vigilance and changes the remembered character judgment.

findings.highlight: You lack experience as a Master.
findings.evidenceJa: 貴方はマスターとして知識がなさすぎる。
findings.governingReading: Saber says Shirou possesses far too little knowledge as a Master.
findings.explanation: Experience changes an immediately remediable information deficit into lack of practice.

findings.highlight: I want you to be stronger.
findings.evidenceJa: シロウには強くなってもらわなければ困ります
findings.governingReading: As his contracted Servant, Saber says she needs Shirou to become stronger.
findings.explanation: Personal desire weakens the necessity and contractual concern in Saber’s formal statement.
